### What to Look for When Choosing an Estate Lawyer

When selecting a firm to assist you with probate in Queensland, consider asking about:

- **Scope of Assistance:** Do you need a "grant-only" service (where the lawyer just handles obtaining the Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration from the Supreme Court of Queensland), or full administration (collecting assets, paying debts, and distributing to beneficiaries)?[[1]](https://jacarandalaw.com.au/probate-and-estate-administration/)
- **Fee Structure:** Ask whether they charge fixed fees for probate grants or hourly rates for ongoing estate administration, plus outlays (such as Supreme Court filing fees and newspaper notices).[[1]](https://jacarandalaw.com.au/probate-and-estate-administration/)
- **Complexity Factors:** If the estate involves superannuation disputes, family provision claims, intestate rules, or foreign assets, look for a firm with dedicated estate litigation experience.[[1]](https://www.fmlaw.com.au/practice-areas/wills-estate-law/)[[2]](https://jacarandalaw.com.au/probate-and-estate-administration/)

If you'd like to share a few details—such as whether there is a **valid will or intestacy** , or if you need **grant-only vs. full estate administration** —I can help you outline the next steps or what documents to prepare.
